instruction: Find all men's medium-size long-sleeve shirts with a discount of 30% or more.

metadata.explanation: Variation 0: Changed size from L to M, discount from 50% to 30%, and sleeve type from short to long. Maintains same complexity and interaction pattern as original task.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical logic error in Price_discount_range parsing: The getter function (chrome.py:2549-2554) only checks for '50_PERCENT_ off & more' and returns 'not_50_PERCENT_ off & more' for all other cases. Expected value is '30_PERCENT_ off & more' which will never match the getter's output
Missing extraction logic for 'long_sleeve' parameter: The getter has short_sleeve_flag logic but no corresponding long_sleeve extraction logic, yet parse_keys expects 'long_sleeve' to be extracted

Semantic verification gap: The evaluator only verifies that the user navigated to a filtered URL but doesn't verify that the filtering actually returned ALL matching items as instructed ('Find all...')
The getter relies on URL path parsing which may be fragile - Macy's URL structure could encode filters differently than expected
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Fix Price_discount_range parsing logic to handle '30_PERCENT_ off & more' correctly - update lines 2549-2554 in get_macys_product_url_parse to parse actual discount values instead of hardcoding 50%
Add extraction logic for 'long_sleeve' parameter similar to how short_sleeve_flag is handled (around line 2522-2539)
Consider whether URL parsing alone is sufficient verification - the task says 'Find all' which implies results should be displayed, not just that filters are applied
Update expected values to match what the getter actually outputs, or fix the getter to output what's expected
